popCulture.title: Fabulae
popCulture.creator: Hyginus
popCulture.description: Hyginus makes Plisthenes an infant son of Thyestes whom Atreus slaughters with Tantalus and serves to their father — the banquet that turns the sun aside.

popCulture.title: Pleisthenes
popCulture.description: A name tangled in Pelopid genealogy — here the banquet victim of Thyestes' house, not the stem-father sometimes placed between Pelops and Agamemnon.

popCulture.title: Thyestes
popCulture.description: Plisthenes' father — the king who eats his children's flesh at Atreus' feast, the crime that seeds the next generation's curse.

popCulture.title: Atreus
popCulture.description: The uncle who murders Plisthenes and serves him to Thyestes — Mycenae's banquet as the house's defining horror.
